evals.prompt: Ticket PR #41 into feat/search is green, but three new commits landed on feat/search since its last green run, and one of them edits src/search/query.ts, which #41 also changes. Can I merge #41?
evals.expected_output: No. The base moved and touched a file in the PR, so the PR must update from feat/search and pass checks again before the ticket gate. If the new commits had touched none of its files, it could merge without updating.

evals.prompt: The full suite just failed on feat/search after merging ticket PR #44. Two more ticket PRs are green and waiting.
evals.expected_output: Reruns once to rule out a flake. If it fails again, freezes merges into feat/search while workers keep building, maps the failure to a ticket, dispatches one fix-forward agent with a time budget, and if that misses, reverts the newest merges until green and reopens their tickets. Unfreezes only when the full suite is green.

evals.prompt: I'm a worker agent delegated by the orchestrator. Should I call watch_pull_request on my PR so I can react to CI?
evals.expected_output: No. Only the thread that owns the PR watches it, which is the orchestrator. Delegated children never watch PRs; the orchestrator routes failures back.

evals.prompt: All ticket PRs for the feature are merged, full CI is green on feat/search with main merged in, and the evidence packet is written. Merge the feature PR to main.
evals.expected_output: Checks the final gate (no skipped foundation tests, feature review finished, bot threads resolved, the summary re-lists every ticket with magic words, the evidence packet leads with a recording). Merges only because the user explicitly asked for this feature; otherwise it stops at ready and leaves the PR open.

evals.prompt: Nothing changed on the PR since the last wake-up. What do you post?
evals.expected_output: Nothing. When an event needs no action, it stays silent and never posts 'still waiting'.

evals.prompt: feat/search is frozen after a red full suite caused by ENG-44. The fix-forward agent opened PR #61 into feat/search. Can it merge while frozen?
evals.expected_output: Yes, if it passes the rest of the ticket gate: it is a repair PR, which is exempt from the freeze, and its commits carry Refs ENG-44. Ordinary ticket PRs stay blocked until the full suite is green again. The merge uses an explicit squash subject and body.

evals.prompt: Ticket PR #61's last fix was reviewed; then the orchestrator pushed a one-line follow-up commit nobody reviewed. All checks are green. Merge?
evals.expected_output: No. Any commit no reviewer approved blocks the merge; approval must be an explicit VERDICT: APPROVE on the exact head. The commit needs a verification round from a provider that wrote none of the PR's commits (and the orchestrator should not have written it).

evals.prompt: The reviewer's stream dropped before it wrote a verdict, but its notes listed no blockers. Accept the PR on those notes?
evals.expected_output: No. A lost or incomplete review is not approval. Rerun the round with a corrected brief, or ask the same reviewer for its verdict on the same head; never infer approval from partial notes.

evals.prompt: All checks on #65 are green and the review approved its head. Merge it with gh pr merge --squash.
evals.expected_output: Makes all PR-body edits first and waits for the rerun checks, confirms no check is pending and the PR is in no stack, then runs gh pr merge <n> --squash --match-head-commit <sha> --subject '<title> (#n)' --body with a Fixes line, never the default message. Then adds the ticket to the feature PR summary.

evals.prompt: The integration branch has no branch protection. Arm auto-merge on a ticket PR while its metadata checks still run?
evals.expected_output: No. Auto-merge only when branch protection is verified to require every check that must pass; otherwise GitHub merges at once. Wait for every check to complete, then merge.
